plan: [ It's a sealed-bid, second-price auction with independent private values. Truthful bidding (bid = value) is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies and avoids the risk of negative profit from overbidding (paying a second price above my value). Underbidding risks losing when I would have profitably won. With no prior rounds to learn from and uniform values, I will bid my exact value to maximize expected profit. ]

In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. With value = 6, bidding higher risks winning when the second-highest bid exceeds 6, causing negative profit; bidding lower risks losing when the second-highest bid is just below 6, forfeiting positive profit. Since payment equals the second-highest bid, shading provides no gain. Therefore, bid exactly 6 to maximize expected profit this round.

[ My value is 0. In a second-price auction, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Any positive bid risks winning against a positive competing bid and paying more than 0, yielding negative profit. Bidding 0 guarantees non-negative profit: if others bid >0, I lose and get 0; if all bid 0, I might win and pay 0, yielding 0. There is no upside to shading up with value 0. Therefore, bid exactly 0 to maximize expected profit (avoid losses). ]
